avis.titre: My Intro To Medicube- Will Repurchase
avis.texte: I was honestly hesitant to buy anything from this brand because it's heavily promoted on TikTok, and I don't usually take influencer reviews too seriously. I know a lot of them are focused on selling rather than giving a genuine opinion. That said, I've been using the Vitamin C Capsule Cream religiously in my morning routine since the end of December, and I've been really impressed. I have normal skin that leans oily, and I just turned 30. I also have some mild hyperpigmentation from not being diligent with sunscreen in my early 20s. The texture of this product is beautiful. Lightweight but still hydrating. It layers perfectly with the rest of my skincare and doesn't pill under sunscreen or makeup, which is huge for me. I also have sensitive skin and was nervous to try another Vitamin C because past ones either broke me out or irritated my skin (Sunday Riley's was the worst for me). Thankfully, this one hasn't caused any irritation or breakouts. Overall, I've noticed my skin tone looks more even, and my texture feels smoother. I love the glow. For me, this has genuinely been a great find.

avis.titre: Not a bad product but deceptive marketing
avis.texte: I've been using this product for a few weeks and the results are perfectly fine for a moisturizer. However I would personally caution against buying this product for the marketing. The whole point of encapsulation is to stabilize ingredients which can easily degrade (in this case Vitamin C), but if you look on the ingredients list you will find ascorbic acid at the very bottom of the list so we know its concentration is less than or equal to 1% which falls far beneath the threshold necessary for the associated claims. And even the other Vitamin C derivatives also have percentages of 1% or lower as evidenced by the fact they are placed below certain ingredients like Ammonium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/​VP Copolymer which are only added in concentrations of around 1%.
